sentences.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a Gram-negative, metabolically versatile bacterium and an opportunistic pathogen of people with serious underlying conditions.
Reported infections include those in cystic fibrosis, burn wounds, immunodeficiency, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and ventilated patients, and it is a leading cause of nosocomial infection.

It survives and persists in various environments and at different stages of pathogenesis through complex regulatory networks and genotypic-phenotypic variation responding to environmental cues and stresses.

Quorum sensing regulates virulence and biofilm formation, the biofilm matrix shields cells from stresses including antibiotics, and biofilm-mediated resistance with persister cells underlies relapse of infections.
Its high intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance makes eradication increasingly difficult, and it is described as an emerging worldwide public health threat.
